_readme: ONE arm: C350, the confirming ingest of the offline chunk benchmark's winner. This is the
ingest-side twin of the offline result in docs/ops/runs/chunk-embed-bench.md (Hermes' run:
production's 1200/100 with mxbai is the worst arm, 94.6% of its chunks past mxbai's real
512-token window; mxbai at 350 tokens beat it by +11.8 pp at recall@10, and with the existing
jina rerank by +17.6 pp; BGE-M3 did not pay for itself). That run measured vector retrieval
only. This one measures the whole pipeline once on the real corpus: graph extraction at the
smaller chunks, mix-mode answers, the frozen probes.
The governing brief is docs/briefs/hermes-chunk350-stack2-ingest.md. Read it before running:
it fixes the pass rule (held-out evidence-in-context up >= 8 pp over production, answerable-
correct not lower beyond the paired CI, refusal accuracy and attribution not lower) and the
rule that the held-out set is scored ONCE, here, for C350 and for the production comparison.
The arm changes exactly two settings; everything else comes from stack2's .env, which the
brief's pre-flight makes equal to production's for every loop-whitelisted name. Do not add
keys: an arm that moves two variables cannot say which one worked. No transcript_prep and no
chunking key on purpose - fixed-token chunking is what the offline winner used, and it applies
to every ingest by itself. COMPANY_AWARE_DEDUPE stays out of this file entirely: do-not-enable.
VERIFY THE NAMES BEFORE THE INGEST, THEN STOP IF THEY ARE WRONG: the LightRAG image's
env.example must spell these settings CHUNK_SIZE and CHUNK_OVERLAP_SIZE. Confirm it, and
confirm the unit while you are there. The request-level chunk key in the 1.5.7 image is
spelled chunk_token_size, and the offline benchmark's 350 was TOKENS (whitespace). If
CHUNK_SIZE turns out to be characters, this arm cuts roughly four times finer than the thing
that won offline and the offline result does not transfer to it - that is a 4x error, not a
rounding detail.
Cross-check the chunk count before trusting anything else: expect roughly 400 chunks from the
10-document corpus (the offline benchmark produced 396-407 at this size). Read it back from
LightRAG after the ingest. If it comes back near ten times that, the arm cut at character
scale; stop and re-read the paragraph above.
The loop recreates the LightRAG service named by --lightrag-service BEFORE it clears or posts
anything, which is what makes the new chunk size take effect for the ingest rather than only
after it. Test coverage: TestChunk350ArmOnStack2 in tests/test_overnight_loop.py.
Run it on stack2, never against production: this file reingests, so it clears the store it
points at. Full explicit flag set, from the repo root, detached, with the pilot's safeguards:
scripts/overnight_loop.py --root ~/rag-project --experiments docs/ops/loop/experiments-chunk350.json
--out ~/rag-project/loop-chunk350 --max-hours 16 --draws 2
--dev-probes probe/solvay-dev-v2.jsonl --heldout-probes probe/solvay-heldout-v2.jsonl
--lightrag-url http://127.0.0.1:9622 --gateway-url http://127.0.0.1:8021
--lightrag-container lightrag-server2 --gateway-container gateway-api2
--lightrag-service lightrag-server2 --gateway-service gateway-api2 --worker-container none
--compose-file ~/rag-project/stack2/compose.yml --compose-project rag-chunk2
--env-file ~/rag-project/stack2/.env
Then score production with the SAME probes, judge and draws, read-only:
scripts/overnight_loop.py --root ~/rag-project --probes-only --arm-name production-1200 \
--out ~/rag-project/loop-chunk350-prod --draws 2 --dev-probes probe/solvay-dev-v2.jsonl \
--heldout-probes probe/solvay-heldout-v2.jsonl
--probes-only needs no --allow-production because it cannot write: no .env write or backup, no
container restart or exec, no compose command, no store clear, no ingest. It reads the target
stack's .env only to find the LightRAG API key, prints the target it is measuring, and issues
only GET /health plus the query and judge POSTs, so production keeps serving while it is scored.
The two arms land in different --out directories, so the paired comparison is made afterwards
with --compare over a merged state, or by hand. Report per arm: chunk count, answerable-correct
%, attribution right/wrong %, refusal accuracy %, evidence-in-context %, probe errors and
latency p50/p95. Keep the recall probe ON: it is what the pass rule is written against.
Docs: docs/briefs/hermes-chunk350-stack2-ingest.md, docs/ops/runs/chunk-embed-bench.md,
docs/09-retrieval-accuracy-plan.md section 4.

experiments.name: C350
experiments._note: The offline winner, confirmed once on the real corpus: 350/50 chunks, everything else as production has it. Fixed-token chunking, no transcript_prep, no chunking key. Reingests, so it only ever runs against stack2.
